stories.title: The Concept of Zombie Firms
stories.description: Ajay explains how weak firms that should fail are artificially kept alive, destroying profitability for healthy firms. Japan's 30-year economic stagnation after 1986 was due to zombie banks keeping zombie firms aloft, which prevented investment and economic dynamism across the entire country.
stories.key_insight: When you artificially preserve failing firms, you damage the entire economy's health and prevent creative destruction from functioning.

stories.title: The Melting Ice Cube Concept
stories.description: When a firm gets into trouble, it rapidly deteriorates like a melting ice cube. Key employees leave, suppliers stop delivering, maintenance is deferred. The faster you intervene with bankruptcy, the more value you preserve from the firm as a going concern.
stories.key_insight: Speed of intervention in bankruptcy is critical - delay destroys intangible capital like organizational culture, relationships, and processes.

recommendations.title: Code 2.0
recommendations.author: Lawrence Lessig
recommendations.why: Shows how law functions as code that shapes how economic machinery runs. Every word in law matters and creates constraints on behavior - foundational for understanding how bankruptcy law restructures incentives.

core_ideas.description: Progress requires both creation AND destruction of firms. Just like Vishnu (creation) and Shiva (destruction) both necessary in Hindu philosophy, the bankruptcy process is essential to clear out non-viable business models.
core_ideas.why_matters: Without understanding destruction as healthy, we become sentimental about failing firms and preserve them artificially, harming the broader economy.

core_ideas.description: In bankruptcy, creditors must negotiate collectively about whether to liquidate or attempt a going concern rescue. This requires business judgment, not just rules-based procedures.
core_ideas.why_matters: India's bankruptcy process struggles because creditors lack commercial sophistication and are heavily influenced by bureaucratic incentives to hide bad news rather than solve problems.

core_ideas.idea: Invisible Infrastructure and Rule of Law
core_ideas.description: Bankruptcy works only when backed by invisible infrastructure: rule of law that actually functions, commercial culture, trust in contracts, independent judiciary.
core_ideas.why_matters: India's IBC is well-designed on paper but fails in implementation due to weak invisible infrastructure - making it a B-grade or C-grade outcome rather than world-class.

jokes_and_cultural_references.moment: When firms are sexually aroused, firms are firm
jokes_and_cultural_references.context: Opening joke about firms and firmness - Amit notes this is the first time Ajay laughed at one of his jokes.
jokes_and_cultural_references.wit: Playful escalation of the word 'firm' across multiple meanings.

jokes_and_cultural_references.context: Amit jokes that Japan not only had zombie firms and zombie banks, they also made great zombie movies. Perhaps we should revisit them for metaphorical art.
jokes_and_cultural_references.wit: Dark humor connecting Japan's economic stagnation to their film genre output.
